title: One Bird Dies, One Flies Free

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the priest shall order that one of the birds be killed over fresh water in a clay pot. He is then to take the live bird and dip it, together with the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn and the hyssop, into the blood of the bird that was killed over the fresh water. Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the defiling disease, and then pronounce them clean. After that, he is to release the live bird in the open fields." - Lev 14:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two birds, identical. One is killed. The other is dipped in the blood of the first, and then set free — released into the open sky, carrying the blood of its companion.

Watch the healed person's face as that bird climbs. That is what has happened to them. Something died so that they could go free.

We should be careful not to press every detail into a code. But Scripture itself teaches us to read the sacrifices this way. They are shadows, and the reality is Christ (Col 2:17; Heb 10:1). And here the shadow falls in a very clear shape: a death, and a release; blood shed, and a life let go.

Christ died once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God (1 Pet 3:18). And what happened to Him did not stay a private event. He was raised, and we are raised with Him. Because he lives, we live.

Notice too the sprinkling — seven times, the number of completeness. Not partially clean. Not clean enough to get by. Thoroughly, finally, completely clean.

If Christ has cleansed you, do not live like a bird still in the priest's hand. The blood has been applied. The sky is open. Go free.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live like someone set free, or still waiting for release?
2. What does "completely clean" stir in you — relief, or disbelief?
3. What would change today if you truly believed the price was fully paid?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You died so that I could go free. Let me live in the open sky of Your finished work rather than in the shadow of my old condition. Amen.
